# ctxray: notes for AI agents

ctxray is an X-ray for agent harnesses. It shows what Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Claude Code Desktop loaded into a model's context (rules, skills, MCP servers and tools, commands, the system prompt, their tokens and why each piece got there), and it lets teams test that in CI. README.md is the shop window, README.RU.md its Russian copy. The manual is the GitHub wiki (https://github.com/MairwunNx/ctxray/wiki).

## Talking to the owner

- Reply in Russian and address the owner as «вы». Quotes «ёлочки», nested „лапки“, an em dash with spaces « — ».
- Code, comments, identifiers, and commit messages are in English. Every string a user sees goes through the i18n catalog (English is the source, Russian ships too). A hard-coded user-facing string is a bug.
- English prose uses curly quotes “ ” and an en dash with spaces ( – ), never an em dash. No semicolons between clauses.

## Hard rules

- **Stack:** Bun + TypeScript (strict) + Elysia, nothing else. Bun is pinned in `package.json` (`packageManager`).
- **Architecture:** Feature-Action Architecture, strictly. Read `Feature-Action-Architecture/AI.md` and `Feature-Action-Architecture/examples/ts-bun.md` (a git submodule, run `git submodule update --init` after cloning).
- **DI:** typed-inject in a functional style. Factories take dependencies as **positional** parameters and declare their tokens:

  ```ts
  export const createInspectAction = (ruleDal: RuleDal, config: Config) => async (cwd: string) => { … };
  createInspectAction.inject = ["ruleDal", "config"] as const;
  ```

  Don't copy the `(deps: Deps) => …` shape from the FAA README: typed-inject passes arguments by position, so it fails typecheck and crashes at runtime. No service classes with state where a function will do, no global singletons. State that lives for a run sits in a closure inside a per-run child injector.
- **Simplest code.** No abstractions “for later”. Explicit beats magic.
- **Small files:** aim for about 120 lines, never more than 200 (i18n catalogs and fixtures excepted). `scripts/check-file-size.ts` fails CI otherwise.
- **Biome** is the only linter and formatter. No ESLint, no Prettier.
- **Unit tests** (`bun:test`) for logic: resolvers, normalisation, harness config parsing, statistics, redaction, locale resolution, plurals, policies, report line rendering, matrix expansion. Skip the trivial. Use `test.each` tables wherever one behaviour meets many inputs, harnesses and locales above all.
- **No telemetry, no network by default.** ctxray talks only to the upstream and registry the user configured.
- **Secrets and PII** never reach traces, logs, reports, or snapshots in clear text. Redaction runs before anything is written to disk.
- **Never touch the user's working tree** during a test run: fixtures and canary markers live in an isolated temporary copy. Harness runs also never touch the user's real `HOME` (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.config/opencode`, `~/.cursor`, the macOS keychain).

## How it fits together

One Bun workspace. `packages/ctxray` is the CLI and the npm package `@mairwunnx/ctxray`. Its `src/` follows FAA:

| Layer | In ctxray |
|---|---|
| `app/` | CLI entry (`main.ts`), command router, DI container (`container.ts`), Elysia app assembly, `Bun.plugin` setup for user test files |
| `features/` | One user-facing use case per CLI command: `inspect`, `test-run`, `diff`, `spectate`, `show-report`, `harness-install`, … Each has `<verb>.action.ts`, a thin `api/command.ts` (parse flags, call the action, hand the result to a renderer) or `api/routes.ts`, and `index.ts` as its public boundary |
| `entities/` | Domain logic two or more features reuse: `harness` (adapter contract and one subfolder per harness), `loadout` (diff, snapshots), `lockfile`, `harness-cache`, `user-config`, `trace` |
| `shared/` | No ctxray domain: `i18n`, `redact`, `tokens`, `markdown` (frontmatter, `@` imports, links), `glob`, `stats`, `render` (Ink and plain), `infra` (fs, process, http, env), and `contract` (the versioned Loadout, Result, and Trace schemas every layer reads) |

Imports go only downward: app → features → entities → shared. Never feature → feature, never entity → entity. Imports keep the `.ts` extension. Another slice or layer comes through its `index.ts` by alias: `#shared/i18n/index.ts`, `#entities/user-config/index.ts` (the `imports` map in `packages/ctxray/package.json`, `#ctxray/*` for root scripts). Inside a slice use `./` or one `../`, never `../../`. No global barrels.

Key concepts, all explained in the wiki: the **Loadout** (everything the agent went into a turn with), the **Loadout Stack** L1 Lint, L2 Policy, L3 Resolve, L4 Assemble, L5 Wire, L6 Activate, L7 Scenario, and the capture **modes** a harness adapter declares: `static` (reads files only), `capture` (ctxray launches the harness and records requests through its proxy), `observe` (the user works, ctxray records through hooks).

## Development

```sh
bun install
bun run check   # biome check, tsc, file size limit
bun test        # unit tests
bun run fix     # biome check --write
```

`PLAN.md`, `docs/adr/`, and `spikes/` are local development notes: they're in `.gitignore` and never get committed.

## Commits and releases

- Conventional Commits in English: `feat(proxy): …`, `fix(i18n): …`, `chore(ci): …`, `docs(wiki): …`. One logical change per commit, and each commit builds and passes its tests.
- `CHANGELOG.md` holds a section per version. The release workflow takes the notes from it.
- GitHub secrets come from the owner's `infrastructure/secrets.toml`. When a step needs a key that isn't there, name it to the owner before the step. Never print a secret's value.
- Before creating another repository, publishing to npm, ghcr, Homebrew, Scoop, or a marketplace, or setting secrets, ask the owner.

# Update dependencies

Bring every pinned version in ctxray up to the newest stable one, prove the project still works, and commit.

If the owner named only some dependencies (`$ARGUMENTS`), update just those.

## What moves together

- **Bun:** `packageManager` in the root `package.json`, `engines.bun` in `packages/ctxray/package.json`, and `@types/bun` (same version as Bun). CI reads Bun from `packageManager`. Install the new Bun locally first (`bun upgrade`), then `bun install` so `bun.lock` follows.
- **Biome:** the `@biomejs/biome` devDependency and the `$schema` URL in `biome.json`. Run `bunx biome migrate --write` after the bump, then `bunx biome check --write .`, and commit the reformat apart from the bump.
- **TypeScript:** the `typescript` devDependency. A new major can tighten checks: fix the code, never loosen `tsconfig.json`.
- **Libraries:** everything `bun outdated` lists, in every workspace package.
- **GitHub Actions:** the `uses:` lines in `.github/workflows/`. Keep pinning the major tag (`actions/checkout@v7`).
- **gitleaks rules:** `VERSION` in `scripts/gen-gitleaks.ts`. Run `bun run gitleaks`, which rewrites `packages/ctxray/src/shared/redact/gitleaks-rules.json`, then `bun test packages/ctxray/src/shared/redact`. A rule that fails to translate stops the script: fix `scripts/lib/go-regex.ts` and add the new syntax to its tests.
- **Feature-Action Architecture:** `git submodule update --remote Feature-Action-Architecture`, then commit the new submodule pointer.
- **Gemma vocabulary:** `packages/ctxray/src/shared/tokens/gemma/` holds Gemma 4's `tokenizer.json` (gzipped) and `tokenizer_config.json` from `google/gemma-4-E2B-it` at the revision `gemma.ts` names. Update it only when Google publishes a newer Gemma tokenizer: download both files at the new revision, gzip the vocabulary, update the revision in the comment, and check that the Gemini CLI counts in `bun test` still hold.
- **Harnesses of the capture fixture:** `packages/ctxray/fixtures/capture/ctxray.lock` pins Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Cursor CLI (Cursor's local build comes from downloads.cursor.com, its version from cursor.com/install). Run `ctxray harness upgrade <name>@<version>` for each in a scratch copy of that folder (with `git init` and a commit), with `CTXRAY_CACHE_DIR` in a scratch folder so nothing lands in the owner's own cache. It prints the loadout diff between the old and the new builds: keep it for the report. Copy the new ctxray.lock back. Then, with the same `CTXRAY_CACHE_DIR`, run `bun scripts/record-payloads.ts <name>` (it takes the builds from the cache by the fixture's lockfile) and `ctxray test -u` in a scratch copy of the fixture, and copy the snapshots back. `bun test` shows what moved in the segmenters' contract tests: fix the segmenter when a marker changed. CI caches the builds by the hash of that lockfile.
- **Harnesses** in general: a new harness version changes what it loads, so loadout snapshots move with it. Upgrade one harness per commit with `ctxray harness upgrade <name>`, read the loadout diff it prints, update the snapshots, and say in the report what changed in the loadout.

## Steps

1. **Read CLAUDE.md**, then run `git status`: leave other people's uncommitted changes alone and keep them out of your commits.
2. **List every pinned version** from the places above, and look for more: `Dockerfile` `FROM` lines, `image:` lines, anything with a version in `.github/`.
3. **Find each newest version** where `sources.md` (next to this file) says to ask. Note old and new side by side. If nothing is behind, say so and stop: no commit, no changelog.
4. **Update in groups,** in this order: Bun, TypeScript, Biome, libraries, gitleaks rules, Actions, the submodule, then each harness. After each group run the check below, so a failure points at its cause.
5. **Majors:** read the release notes or the migration guide and fix the code. If a major breaks too much to fix well, keep the old major and say so in the report.
6. **Check:** `bun install && bun run check && bun test`. When Bun moved, also build the compiled binary and run its smoke test, once they exist: user test files reach the binary through `Bun.plugin` with `build.module`, which Bun doesn't document and may change.
7. **Changelog:** when an update reaches what ctxray ships (the CLI, the npm package, the image, the plugin), add a line to the topmost `CHANGELOG.md` section that isn't released yet (`gh release view vX.Y.Z` fails), or open a new section with the next patch version. Updates that only touch CI or development tools need none.
8. **Commit and push,** one commit per group, in Conventional Commits: `chore(deps): update Bun to 1.4.5`, `chore(deps): update Biome to 2.7.0`, `chore(ci): update actions/checkout to v8`.

## Running unattended

The weekly autopilot (`.github/workflows/autopilot.yml`) runs this with nobody to answer. Where a step would ask the owner, take the choice that keeps the project working as it does today and name it in the report. A failure you can't fix stays out of the commit: keep the old version and go on with the rest.

# ctxray


🩻 **ctxray** is an X-ray for agent harnesses. It shows what Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or OpenCode loaded into the model: rules, skills, MCP tools, the system prompt, and the tokens each one costs. Then it checks that in CI, so a broken rule never reaches your team. [Русская версия](https://github.com/MairwunNx/ctxray/blob/master/README.RU.md) > [!WARNING] > ctxray is in early development, and nothing is released yet. Until 1.0, minor versions may change the API. ## What you get - 🔍 **See what the agent loaded.** `ctxray inspect` lists the rules, skills, MCP servers and their tools, commands, and the system prompt your agent works with in this repository. - 🪙 **Tokens for every piece.** Each rule, skill, and MCP server shows its token count, so you know what fills the context. Estimates are marked ≈, and counts are exact when the model provider counts them. - ❓ **Why it's there.** Every piece says why it loaded: it's always on, a file path matched, or the model asked for it. - ✅ **Tests for your agent setup.** `*.ctxray.ts` files read like Bun or Vitest tests: “payment rules load for payment code”, “the context stays under 25k tokens”, “this prompt picks the refunds skill”. - 🧪 **One test, every agent.** The same test runs against each agent you use. You don't copy it per tool. - 🎯 **Does the model pick the right skill?** A prompt runs a few dozen times against a real model, and ctxray reports how often the skill loaded, with a confidence interval. Record the answers once, and every merge request replays them for free. - 📉 **What a merge request changes.** `ctxray diff` compares with the main branch: a new MCP server with 14 tools, a rule that grew by 6k tokens. - 📋 **Your organisation's rules.** Token limits, banned MCP servers, a required AGENTS.md: checked on every merge request, without calling a model. - 🏢 **Works in a closed network.** Corporate LLM gateways, proxies, your own CA certificates, and internal npm registries all work. - 🔒 **Secrets stay out.** API keys, tokens, emails, phone and card numbers are hidden before anything is written to disk. - 📊 **Reports for people and for CI.** A live view in the terminal, an HTML report, JUnit, Allure, JSON, and a short Markdown summary for the merge request. - 🌍 **English and Russian.** ctxray picks your system's language, or the one you pass with `--lang`. ## Supported agents ctxray reads each agent's files without launching it. Where the agent allows it, ctxray can also launch the agent and record its requests to the model, or record a session you run yourself. | Agent | Reads files | Launches and records | Records your session | |---|:-:|:-:|:-:| | Claude Code | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | Codex | ✓ | ✓ | | | Gemini CLI | ✓ | ✓ | | | OpenCode | ✓ | ✓ | | | Cursor CLI | ✓ | experimental | ✓ | | Cursor (editor) | ✓ | | ✓ | | Claude Code Desktop | ✓ | | ✓ | ## The Loadout Stack ctxray checks your agent setup in seven layers, from cheap to expensive. The first three only read files. The rest launch the agent. | Layer | What it checks | |---|---| | L1 Lint | The rule, skill, and config files are valid | | L2 Policy | The setup follows your organisation's rules | | L3 Resolve | The right rules apply to the files you work on | | L4 Assemble | The agent really sent them to the model | | L5 Wire | The agent adds the right rule when it reads a file or calls a skill | | L6 Activate | The model picks the right skill for a prompt | | L7 Scenario | The agent gets the task done the right way | ## Get started These commands work from the first release on. 1. See what your agent loads: ```sh bunx @mairwunnx/ctxray inspect ``` 2. Create a config and an example test with `ctxray init`. 3. Run `ctxray test` locally, then add it to CI. ## Documentation The [wiki](https://github.com/MairwunNx/ctxray/wiki) holds the manual. It grows with ctxray. ## Related projects - **[Feature-Action Architecture](https://github.com/MairwunNx/Feature-Action-Architecture)** – the architecture ctxray's code follows. - **[Allay AI](https://allay.chat)** – an AI helper for Minecraft servers that answers players from their real game. ## Content disclosures - 🤖 **AI-generated code.** AI agents wrote much of the code. - 📡 **No telemetry.** ctxray sends nothing about you anywhere. # Where fresh versions come from

Ask the source, never your memory: versions move every week. Take the newest **stable** version. Skip anything marked alpha, beta, rc, canary, next, dev, insiders, or preview, unless the project already uses that channel.

Compare versions as numbers, part by part: 1.10 is newer than 1.9. A list sorted as text can name an older version.

| What | Where to ask | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bun | `gh api repos/oven-sh/bun/releases/latest -q .tag_name` | Tags read `bun-v1.4.4`. `@types/bun` takes the same version |
| npm packages | `bun outdated`, `npm view <package> version` | `npm view <package> dist-tags` shows the channels. TypeScript's `latest` tag is the stable one |
| Biome | `npm view @biomejs/biome version` | The `biome.json` schema URL carries the version |
| GitHub Actions | `gh api repos/<owner>/<action>/releases/latest -q .tag_name` | Pin the major tag |
| gitleaks rules | `gh api repos/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/latest -q .tag_name` | Tags read `v8.30.1` |
| Feature-Action Architecture | `git ls-remote https://github.com/MairwunNx/Feature-Action-Architecture.git HEAD` | The submodule follows the default branch |
| Claude Code | `npm view @anthropic-ai/claude-code version` | Native builds come from `downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/<version>/<platform>/claude`, with checksums in that version's `manifest.json` |
| Codex | `npm view @openai/codex version` | One npm launcher plus per-platform packages |
| Gemini CLI | `npm view @google/gemini-cli version` | |
| OpenCode | `npm view opencode-ai version` | One npm wrapper plus per-platform binaries |
| Cursor CLI | `curl -fsS https://cursor.com/install` | The script names the current build in its `downloads.cursor.com/lab/<version>/…` URL. Read it, never pipe it into a shell |
